expertNames: Gerald Shargel, Ellen Yaroshefsky, Lisa Wayne, Chris Voss, BJ Fogg

intake.situation: I'm a CFO who got indicted for wire fraud along with two co-workers. My public defender seems competent but overwhelmed — he handles mostly drug cases and I'm not sure he understands white collar defense. He hasn't discussed discovery even though the government seized my work laptop and financial records months ago. I don't even know what they have on me.
intake.specific_question: Can they use my work emails against me? I sent hundreds of emails about the transactions they're calling fraud — but at the time I believed everything was legitimate business. Does intent matter?

phase2_data.attorney_firm: Federal Public Defender's Office, Northern District of California
phase2_data.biggest_concern: I could go to federal prison. I have a 12-year-old daughter. My ex-husband will use this to take full custody. I can't lose her.
phase2_data.what_attorney_told: He said the government has a strong case but there might be room to negotiate. He hasn't explained what that means.
phase2_data.employment: Terminated as CFO after indictment — currently unemployed, living on savings
phase2_data.dependents: One daughter (age 12), shared custody with ex-husband
